prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” lawyer — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your case (severity of injuries, who was at fault, whether a commercial carrier is involved, available evidence, deadlines). I can help you find a great Dallas lawyer, but first here’s how to pick one and what to do right now.

How to pick the best Dallas truck-accident lawyer
- Look for dedicated truck-accident or catastrophic-injury experience (not just general PI). Trucking cases involve FMCSA rules, logbooks, carrier defenses and expert witnesses.
- Trial experience and results: ask about verdicts/settlements in truck or commercial-vehicle cases, not just car-crash claims.
- Resources: firm should have investigators, accident-reconstruction and medical experts, and experience dealing with big trucking companies and insurers.
- Communication and availability: who will handle day-to-day work, how often they’ll update you.
- Fees and costs: most work on contingency — get the percentage, who pays upfront costs, and how liens are handled.
- Reputation: peer reviews (Super Lawyers), client reviews, state-bar standing, and AVVO/Google ratings.
- Local courtroom experience: familiarity with Dallas courts and judges is useful.

Questions to ask at a free consult
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against interstate carriers? Do you use accident-reconstruction experts?
- What results have you obtained in similar cases (without breaching client confidentiality)?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What is your estimate of my case’s timeline and value?

Immediate steps to protect your claim
- Get medical treatment and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicle/scene, police report, witness contact info, truck’s logbook, carrier name, license plate, DOT number, dashcam/phone video.
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers or sign releases without counsel.
- Preserve devices and phone data; don’t post details on social media.
- Note Texas statute of limitations: typically two years from the crash date for personal injury.

How I can help right now
- If you want, tell me your Dallas ZIP or neighborhood, accident date, and any key facts (serious injuries, commercial truck, police report filed). I can:
  - Search and shortlist 3–5 Dallas attorneys/firms with documented truck-accident experience and recent results.
  - Draft a short message you can send to firms to speed up consultations.

Would you like me to find a short list of Dallas truck-accident lawyers now? If so, share your ZIP or a few case details.
